title: Abbreviation clues
summary: These clues tell you—sometimes quietly—that the answer will be shortened.
explanation: “Briefly” changes the expected answer from SPECIFICATION to its familiar four-letter shortening, SPEC.
advice: Match the clue's level of shortening. If the clue contains an abbreviation, the answer often does too.

title: Direct-definition clues
summary: The clue and answer are close synonyms or a simple category-and-member pair.
explanation: Both are base-form verbs with the same meaning, so crossings and answer length do the disambiguating.
advice: Check grammar before reaching for obscure synonyms. A plural clue usually needs a plural answer; past tense usually stays past tense.

title: Question-mark clues
summary: A question mark often warns that the clue is playful, indirect, or using an unexpected sense.
signals: a literal reading that feels wrong
explanation: “Strike” shifts from its everyday senses to bowling, where a strike happens in an alley.
advice: List two or three meanings of the clue's most noticeable noun or verb. The answer often lives in the less obvious one.

title: Fill-in-the-blank clues
summary: The answer completes a familiar phrase, title, quotation, or name.
explanation: The fixed phrase “ebb and flow” supplies the missing word directly.
advice: Read the completed phrase aloud. Crossings help when several words could sound natural.

title: Names and fact clues
summary: These clues rely on a person, place, title, brand, or piece of general knowledge.
explanation: The quoted work and performer role identify the artist; the answer length confirms the fit.
advice: Use every qualifier. Decade, nationality, medium, and quoted title are there to narrow a large name set.
